clue.text: Hopeless sort of counsel?

parts.note: plays on the set phrase 'counsel of ...' for advice given when all hope is gone, so the hopeless sort of counsel names the state itself

explanation.walkthrough: The 'counsel of despair' is advice that assumes nothing can be done; the clue reads counsel as a lawyer to mislead.
explanation.definitionFit: Despair is utter loss of hope, which is what the hopeless counsel phrase expresses.

clue.text: Detective may be spotted eating

definitions.meaning: a private eye, in slang a private investigator
spotted ... is a British steamed suet pudding studded with currants, so something spotted you may be eating

explanation.walkthrough: Spotted dick is a traditional British currant pudding; the surface suggests a detective caught out while having lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: Dick is slang for a private investigator, and also the second word of a currant pudding's name.

clue.text: Walk with difficulty, going to intermingle

definitions.meaning: to drag the feet along in a slow, awkward gait
to mix things up together, as cards are mixed before dealing

explanation.surface: Someone limps along to join in mingling at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To shuffle is both to walk dragging the feet and to mix cards or items together.

clue.text: Fine waived out of consideration for player

indicators.note: a fine that is waived is let off, so the letter for fine is dropped from the word

parts.note: a factor is a consideration taken into account
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A penalty is let off because of some consideration on behalf of a sportsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A player is someone who performs a part on stage, a synonym for a thespian.

clue.text: Mountain with faces famous through history

definitions.text: Mountain with faces famous through history

parts.words: Mountain with faces famous through history
parts.note: describes the South Dakota peak carved with four huge heads of US presidents, faces famous in history

explanation.walkthrough: Mount Rushmore in South Dakota bears carved heads of Washington, Jefferson, Theodore Roosevelt and Lincoln; 'faces' is literal, not climbers' rock faces.
explanation.definitionFit: The American mountain is carved with the faces of four celebrated presidents.

clue.text: Grumble, plot being hard to decipher

parts.note: to crab is to complain or grumble
a bed is a plot of garden ground

explanation.surface: A complaint that a story's plot is too difficult to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabbed handwriting is cramped and difficult to read, so hard to make out.

clue.text: Not a gentleman to hold an area in the country

indicators.note: the first word is made to hold the next one inside it

parts.note: a cad is a man who behaves dishonourably, no gentleman
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bounder is found to have grabbed some land in a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Canada is a country of North America, so it fits the country as an example.

clue.text: Be proud of Times workers coming in for little extra

indicators.note: the two short pieces come into the middle of the longer word

parts.note: to admire is to regard with pride or approval
X is the multiplication sign, read as 'times'
TU is a trade union, a body of workers

explanation.surface: Staff at The Times newspaper take pride in a small bonus coming their way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but is the multiplication sign X.
explanation.definitionFit: An admixture is a small quantity of something added in, a little extra ingredient.

clue.text: Finance house crook held up for bread

indicators.note: the bank holds the other piece within it

parts.note: a bank is an institution handling money

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a con is a swindler or crook, short for con man

explanation.surface: A dishonest banker is robbed for money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held up' reads as a robbery but splits: 'held' is the container and 'up' turns the crook word around in this down entry. A bannock is a flat Scottish loaf.
explanation.definitionFit: A bannock is a round flat loaf of oatmeal or barley, a kind of Scottish bread.

clue.text: Put hair in these? Houdini didn't

definitions.text: Put hair in these? Houdini didn't

parts.words: Put hair in these? Houdini didn't
parts.note: a hairstyle of matted ropes, read as fearsome locks which the famous escapologist never feared

explanation.walkthrough: Split as 'dread locks': Houdini, the escape artist, did not dread locks.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreadlocks are hair twisted into long ropes, and the split phrase means fearing padlocks.

clue.text: Mistress deciphering old Etruscan

indicators.note: deciphering works the letters out into a new order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A scholar's mistress is translating an ancient Etruscan text.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtesan is a kept mistress of a wealthy man, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Cut to pieces, caught in explosive device

indicators.note: one piece sits in the other

parts.note: a mine is a buried explosive device
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone is blown apart, caught by a landmine.
explanation.definitionFit: To mince is to chop into very small pieces, as with meat.

clue.text: Novelist showing ex-president very keen at university

parts.note: Gerald Ford was a former US president
mad about something means extremely enthusiastic
Oxford is the English university

explanation.surface: A writer is showing a former head of state to be a keen academic.
explanation.definitionFit: Ford Madox Ford was an English novelist, author of The Good Soldier and Parade's End.

clue.text: Extensive range available in lilac or red

indicators.note: the letters are made available to be put to use in a new order

explanation.surface: A wide selection of colours is offered in lilac or red.
explanation.definitionFit: A cordillera is an extensive chain of mountains, such as the Andes, which is a range.

clue.text: But Liege wasn't the target of this European assault

definitions.text: But Liege wasn't the target of this European assault

parts.words: But Liege wasn't the target of this European assault
parts.note: a liege is a feudal lord, while the 1944 Allied landing operation in Normandy bore that name though Liège in Belgium was not its target

explanation.walkthrough: Operation Overlord was the 1944 invasion of Normandy; a liege is a feudal superior, but the Belgian city Liège was not the target.
explanation.definitionFit: The codename for the D-Day invasion also means a feudal lord, which is a liege.

clue.text: Drop in on person, and appear at advantage

definitions.meaning: to pay someone a casual visit
read literally, to seem one point ahead

explanation.surface: Calling on a friend makes a good impression.
explanation.definitionFit: To look someone up is to visit them; to look one up is to appear a point ahead.

clue.text: Bats counting as bird? Yes and no

definitions.meaning: a bird known for laying its eggs in others' nests

explanation.surface: Should bats count as birds? The answer is both yes and no.
explanation.walkthrough: Bats are not birds, yet the answer means both 'bats' (mad) and a bird, hence 'Yes and no'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuckoo is slang for crazy and is also the name of a well-known bird.

clue.text: Intervals in US play announced in our pages

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other

parts.note: the clue is printed in The Times, so its pages are the Times
news that is out has been made public

explanation.surface: Breaks in an American game are reported in this newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'our pages' is the setter's own newspaper, The Times, and 'announced' means made public; the second piece sits before the paper's final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Time-outs are short breaks called during American sports games, so they are intervals.

clue.text: Cavalryman dropping one old battleaxe

indicators.note: the cavalryman drops a letter, losing it

parts.note: a dragoon is a mounted soldier
O resembles the numeral 0, used here for one

explanation.surface: A horse soldier drops an ancient weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'battleaxe' suggests a weapon but means a formidable woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragon, like a battleaxe, is a fierce and domineering older woman.

clue.text: A nobleman talked of credit arrangement

indicators.note: the words are spoken, signalling a soundalike

parts.note: a count is a European nobleman

explanation.surface: An aristocrat discusses a loan arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: An account is an arrangement with a bank or shop allowing credit.

clue.text: Blow on flank giving mate

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it

parts.note: a side is a flank
a kick is a blow with the foot

explanation.surface: A strike to the side brings down a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidekick is a close companion or assistant, a mate.

clue.text: At the wicket, supervised youngsters: not out!

parts.note: a cricket batsman at the wicket is in
wards are minors placed under a guardian

explanation.surface: At cricket, the children batting are given not out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not out' looks like an umpire's verdict but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Inwards means towards the inside, the opposite of out.

clue.text: Violent tale captivating millions

indicators.note: the story holds the other piece captive inside

parts.note: a story is a tale

explanation.surface: A gripping story about brutality enthrals millions.
explanation.definitionFit: Stormy weather or relations are violent and turbulent.

clue.text: Lots involved in undeserved success?

parts.note: success that comes from drawing lots rather than merit, a phrase for chance outcomes

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lots' is not 'a great deal' but lots drawn by chance.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means pure chance, as in drawing lots, so success unearned by skill.

clue.text: One may follow this for pop broadcasts

definitions.text: One may follow this for pop broadcasts

parts.words: One may follow this for pop broadcasts
parts.note: the BBC pop station is named with the word 'One' after the medium, so one follows it

explanation.walkthrough: BBC Radio 1 is Britain's national pop music station; the numeral one literally follows the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio is the broadcasting medium, and BBC Radio 1 is the UK pop station.

clue.text: Knocks up box

definitions.meaning: practises with light exchanges, as players warm up before a match

explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to practise boxing or to exchange practice blows, warming up.

clue.text: Avoid bawdy talk, English

indicators.note: said in talk, so the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: lewd means bawdy or crude

explanation.surface: Keep clear of smutty English conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: To elude is to escape or avoid, as in evading capture.

clue.text: Not straight progress, collecting drinks from the bar?

definitions.meaning: a journey out and back again rather than one in a straight line
a trip to fetch a set of drinks bought for the whole group

explanation.surface: A meandering walk to the bar to pick up everyone's drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a 'round' is a set of drinks bought for a group, so fetching it is a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A round trip is a journey out and back, and also, punningly, a trip for a round of drinks.

clue.text: No quick check here of wrong payouts

indicators.note: the letters are put wrong, in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Faulty payouts get only a slow inspection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quick' means living (as in 'the quick and the dead'): a post-mortem examines someone no longer quick. 'wrong' rearranges PAYOUTS.
explanation.definitionFit: An autopsy is a post-mortem examination, a check on someone no longer living.

clue.text: Thoroughly search round wrong corner of country for this Northerner

indicators.note: the search word goes round the other piece

parts.note: to scour is to search thoroughly
SE is south-east, the opposite corner of England from Liverpool in the north-west

explanation.surface: A thorough hunt in the wrong part of England for a man from the North.
explanation.walkthrough: A Scouser is someone from Liverpool, in England's north-west; SE (south-east) is the wrong corner for them.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scouser is a native of Liverpool, a city in the north of England.
